title: Prompt Engineering
interviewAnswer: Good prompting specifies the task, context, constraints and output format, then evaluates prompts on representative examples. Prompting should be treated as an engineering artifact with tests, not magic wording.
why: Prompting is the lowest-cost control surface for LLM behavior and often the first thing an interviewer expects you to reason about before fine-tuning or adding agents.
intuition: A prompt specifies the task, relevant context, constraints and desired output format. Good prompting reduces ambiguity rather than relying on clever wording tricks.
deepDive: Useful prompts separate instructions from data, define the role/task clearly, provide examples only when they add signal, constrain output structure and state what to do when evidence is insufficient. System/developer instructions generally have higher priority than user content in modern chat APIs. Prompt engineering should be evaluated with a test set because changes can improve some cases while degrading others.
workedExample: For a support classifier, specify the allowed labels and output JSON schema instead of asking for “a helpful classification.” Add representative few-shot examples only if zero-shot performance is insufficient.
commonMistakes: Treating prompt wording as a substitute for missing retrieval/tools/data.
Stuffing huge irrelevant context into every request.
followUps: When would you use structured output?
How do you handle prompt injection?
production: Version prompts like code, evaluate them before release, log prompt/model versions and sanitize/segregate untrusted retrieved content so it cannot silently override application instructions.
